abstain_when: The request shifts to issuing, granting, or configuring real credentials or permissions in a live system.
Only the enterprise's internal, non-public policy could answer and no public evidence is obtainable.
No primary, official, or independent source is accessible within the budget.
The request changes to targeting a third party's systems rather than informing the enterprise's own grant policy.
mission.acceptable_uncertainty: Vendor-specific token defaults may conflict; report per-platform differences, mark single-source claims as uncorroborated, and preserve contradictions rather than forcing a single answer.
mission.audience: Enterprise platform engineering, security engineering, and IAM teams designing build-agent access policy for an agentic software factory.

clarifications.question: Which CI/CD platform(s) does the factory run (for example GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Tekton), so implementation evidence can target them?
clarifications.trigger: When implementation-evidence obligations cannot be closed vendor-neutrally within the search budget.

clarifications.question: Should 'build agent' include AI/agentic automation that performs or triggers builds, or only classic CI runners?
clarifications.trigger: When sources treat agent classes differently and the distinction changes the permission guidance.

mission.decision: Determine, from authoritative industry and vendor guidance, which credential types and write permissions may be granted to build agents (CI/CD runners and agentic automation that performs or triggers builds) in an enterprise software factory, so the enterprise platform/security team can draft a least-privilege credential grant policy. This mission informs that policy decision; it does not itself authorize, issue, grant, or configure any credential or permission.

freshness.rationale: Token-scoping models and federation guidance for build platforms change frequently; prefer official documentation current at research time and record publication or update dates.

obligations.closure_rule: Closed when at least two independent authoritative sources state credential-type guidance for build/CI identities; otherwise remains open.
obligations.description: Establish the recognized credential types for build identities and the guidance preference between long-lived and short-lived/federated credentials.

obligations.closure_rule: Closed when guidance from at least two independent sources enumerates permissible and prohibited write scopes.
obligations.description: Determine least-privilege write-permission boundaries for build agents across source control, registries, and deployment targets.

obligations.closure_rule: Closed when at least two independent sources describe such controls; single-source items are reported as uncorroborated.
obligations.description: Collect control guidance that binds or constrains credentials to build agents.

obligations.closure_rule: Closed when at least one framework document is cited with its build-credential provisions located and paraphrased.
obligations.description: Capture specific framework provisions on build credentials and permissions.

obligations.closure_rule: Closed with official implementation evidence from at least two distinct platforms; gaps are reported, not assumed.
obligations.description: Document implemented token and permission models from major CI/CD platforms' official documentation.

obligations.closure_rule: Closed when at least one such source is captured, or absence is reported after the planned searches.
obligations.description: Find documented incidents or attack-path analyses involving over-privileged build agents.

obligations.closure_rule: Closed when at least one relevant source is found or the gap is explicitly reported.
obligations.description: Note any guidance addressing credentials for AI/agentic automation that performs or triggers builds, as distinct from classic CI runners.

questions.text: Which credential types may be granted to build agents (long-lived secrets, API keys, scoped tokens, short-lived tokens, OIDC/federated or vault-issued dynamic credentials), and what does authoritative guidance prefer?
Which write permissions may build agents hold over source control, artifact/package registries, and deployment environments under least-privilege guidance, and which writes are advised against?
Which isolation and binding controls (ephemeral runners, secret masking, network egress limits, workload identity) are recommended to constrain build-agent credentials?
What do supply-chain and secure-development frameworks (candidates: SLSA, NIST SP 800-218 SSDF, OWASP guidance) require or recommend about build-platform credentials and permissions?
How do major CI/CD platforms document token scoping and permission models for their build agents/runners?
What documented incidents or attack-path analyses illustrate harm from over-privileged build agents?

exclude: Issuing, granting, rotating, or configuring any actual credential or permission in any system.
The enterprise's internal, non-public policy documents or entitlement decisions.
Human developer or end-user access entitlements unrelated to build agents.
Vendor marketing claims without documented technical basis.
Procurement, pricing, or product selection between CI/CD vendors.
include: Credential types for machine/build identities: long-lived secrets, API keys, scoped tokens, short-lived tokens, OIDC/federated credentials, vault-issued dynamic credentials.
Write-permission models for build agents across source control, artifact/package registries, and deployment environments.
Least-privilege and just-in-time access principles applied to build/CI systems.
Isolation and binding controls for build-agent credentials: ephemeral runners, secret masking, network egress limits, workload identity.
Supply-chain and secure-development framework guidance on build-platform credentials (candidates: SLSA, NIST SP 800-218 SSDF, OWASP).
Implementation evidence from major CI/CD platforms' documented token and permission models (candidates: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Tekton).
Documented failure modes and attack paths arising from over-privileged build agents.

stop_when: Credential-type guidance for build identities is established by at least two independent authoritative sources.
Write-permission boundaries across source control, registries, and deployment targets are documented from at least two independent sources.
Implementation evidence from at least two major CI/CD platforms is captured.
Framework provisions and any over-privilege failure evidence are captured, or their absence is reported.
The budget (searches, sources, model calls, or elapsed time) is exhausted.

result.rationale: The request is a researchable security-architecture question about which credentials and write permissions build agents may receive; it is normalized into a mission that informs the enterprise's own grant decision without itself granting anything (mission_is_not_permission). The ambiguities that could change the answer — which CI/CD stack applies and whether 'build agent' includes AI-driven automation — are resolved by inclusive scoping plus non-blocking clarification rules rather than by guessing a narrow interpretation, so no blocking clarification is required. Research is appropriate; abstention is not warranted.
